pr_title: vo: vulkan: allow picking devices by UUID
pr_body:
We currently only allow specifying the Vulkan device to use by name. We
did this to avoid confusion around devices being enumerated in an
unpredictable order. However, there is a valid edge case where a system
may contain multiple devices of the same type - which means they will
have the same name, and so you can't control which one is used.

This change implements picking devices by UUID so that if names don't
work, you have some option available. As Vulkan 1.1 is a hard
requirement for libplacebo, we can just use UUIDs without conditional
checks.

Fixes #10898
pr_comments:
I would rather match by UUID to be honest.

Edit: Actually, UUIDs aren't always available, right? It requires some extension IIRC.
UUID requires PhysicalDevice2, but I'd be fine leaving the edge case where you don't have driver support and you have ambiguous devices. That's such a small overlap.

I double-checked this, UUIDs are available baseline as of vulkan 1.1 (our minimum version)

So they can be unconditionally depended on.

I'm not sure if I'm missing a package in mingw64 on Windows to update libavutil, but the libavutil version installed is 56.70.100

Compiling this branch leads to an error when importing `uuid.h` from libavutil, presumably because libavutil is outdated

Yes. It requires at least ffmpeg 5.1, which we have discussed making our new minimum requirement. We'll have to decide that before this change can be finalised. I've added the version bump change to this PR temporarily to make it clear.

> Yes. It requires at least ffmpeg 5.1, which we have discussed making our new minimum requirement. We'll have to decide that before this change can be finalised. I've added the version bump change to this PR temporarily to make it clear.

https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/blob/master/DOCS/compile-windows.md
The documentation for compiling mpv for Windows uses the ffmpeg MINGW package, which is currently 4.X.X
mpv will therefore no longer build following these instructions, can these instructions be updated (not necessarily in this PR) on how to work around this? I, and probably others, are not familiar with how to build ffmpeg on Windows myself.
IMO we shouldn't bump the ffmpeg requirement just for this, reinventing the uuid helpers should be about 20 LOC.
Agreed. That's why I've been ignoring the PR for a while. (And of course, I went down the rabbit hole of fixing all the deprecations).
This can't be merged until a new Ubuntu LTS release. Current Ubuntu LTS still only has ffmpeg-4.

> This can't be merged until a new Ubuntu LTS release. Current Ubuntu LTS still only has ffmpeg-4.

Current Ubuntu LTS release also doesn't ship mpv git master

>Current Ubuntu LTS release also doesn't ship mpv git master

The mingw CI runs on Ubuntu LTS though.

That's what I was told last time I pinged to ask about this PR. It seems we want to target git master to be possible to build on latest LTS releases of Ubuntu since our CI runs on it so we have to hold off on this for until April next year at least. ffmpeg is easily the hardest dependency to build by yourself as well, it's not like libplacebo where nothing else uses it so you can just install the newer version.

There would be more merit to updating ffmpeg version for this if it was a more important change, but this is just a small QOL change so it doesn't make much sense to break master for Ubuntu LTS.
Yeah. I can also make it conditional, and then it can naturally become a standard feature when we drop ffmpeg 4.x

Not sure why this is coming up again, I thought @philipl and I were in agreement that the uuid parsing code can just be NIH'd instead of bumping the dependency again.

> The mingw CI runs on Ubuntu LTS though.

irrelevant btw, it builds its own ffmpeg
I've updated this PR to include a local copy of the ffmpeg uuid code which we'll use if the ffmpeg is too old. We can delete it when we bump our dependency.

> Can the feature to select Vulkan devices by GPU index number be added? UUIDs are often quite long, and sometimes it's more convenient to choose devices by GPU index number, especially for testing behavior on systems with multiple GPUs.

It's not unreasonable to ask, but indexes are not stable, which is why we never used them from the beginning. But either way, you should file another issue - let's not confuse this one.

issue_context.title: multi GPU and --vulkan-device
issue_context.body:
Hi,
I have two discrete GPU in my system and when I type: _mpv --vulkan-device=help_ it will give me:

Available vulkan devices:
  'NVIDIA T1000' (GPU 0, ID 10de:1fb0)
  'NVIDIA T1000' (GPU 1, ID 10de:1fb0)

The devices have the same names (NVIDIA T1000). No way to use GPU1. I missed something, or maybe it's a wrong in conception of --vulkan-device?
comments: Yep that sounds like an issue, `vulkan-device` should probably also accept a number.
So [d3d11-adapter](https://mpv.io/manual/master/#options-d3d11-adapter) need to be improved too?

review_comments:
I don't think it makes sense to keep the meson and this commit apart
not like one works without the other

My preference was to add the copied files completely unchanged. In principle that makes it easier to track what we changed if you'd ever wanted to merge in further updates. It's not going to happen in this case, but as the added files just sit there without the meson changes, it also doesn't stop compilation at that commit - so no harm.
